text: Patched, not rebuilt. How a ligament heals after a sprain, and why it is different from muscle.
spoken: Patched, not rebuilt. How a ligament heals after a sprain, and why it is different from muscle.

text: Muscle and ligament go through the same repair steps.
spoken: Muscle and ligament go through the same repair steps.

text: But only one of them can actually rebuild itself.
spoken: But only one of them can actually rebuild itself.

text: The other patches the hole with scar, and it never fully goes back to the original.
spoken: The other patches the hole with scar, and it never fully goes back to the original.

text: A ligament is mostly type I collagen, arranged in tight parallel bundles.
spoken: A ligament is mostly type one collagen, arranged in tight parallel bundles.

text: It has very few cells and a poor blood supply.
spoken: It has very few cells and a poor blood supply.

text: Most of its vessels, nerves, and backup cells live in the outer layer, the epiligament.
spoken: Most of its vessels, nerves, and backup cells live in the outer layer, the epiligament.

text: Ligaments also contain mechanoreceptors that tell the brain where the joint is.
spoken: Ligaments also contain mechanoreceptors that tell the brain where the joint is.

text: Clinical tie-in. Compared with muscle.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Compared with muscle.

text: Muscle is packed with blood vessels and has satellite cells under every fiber.
spoken: Muscle is packed with blood vessels and has satellite cells under every fiber.

text: Ligament has neither, so it has to recruit help from outside.
spoken: Ligament has neither, so it has to recruit help from outside.

text: Stecco link: the epiligament plays the same role for ligament that the epimysium and deep fascia play for muscle. It is the gliding, vessel-rich, cell-supplying envelope.
spoken: Stecco link: the epiligament plays the same role for ligament that the epimysium and deep fascia play for muscle. It is the gliding, vessel-rich, cell-supplying envelope.

text: When the fibers snap, the ligament cells lose the tension they depend on, and many of them die within hours.
spoken: When the fibers snap, the ligament cells lose the tension they depend on, and many of them die within hours.

text: Bleeding comes mostly from the torn epiligament.
spoken: Bleeding comes mostly from the torn epiligament.

text: Unlike muscle, there's no contraction band to seal anything.
spoken: Unlike muscle, there's no contraction band to seal anything.

text: That is a muscle-fiber feature only.
spoken: That is a muscle-fiber feature only.

text: Grade I: stretched fibers.
spoken: Grade one: stretched fibers.

text: Grade II: a partial tear.
spoken: Grade two: a partial tear.

text: Grade III: a complete tear, with joint laxity.
spoken: Grade three: a complete tear, with joint laxity.

text: The first five days look almost exactly like muscle:
spoken: The first five days look almost exactly like muscle:

text: clot, growth factors, and a flood of neutrophils.
spoken: clot, growth factors, and a flood of neutrophils.

text: The fibrin clot becomes the temporary scaffold that everything else will build on.
spoken: The fibrin clot becomes the temporary scaffold that everything else will build on.

text: Clinical tie-in. Protect the scaffold.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Protect the scaffold.

text: Protect, compress, elevate.
spoken: Protect, compress, elevate.

text: For a Grade III ankle sprain, a short period of rigid support, 10 days or less, is reasonable.
spoken: For a Grade three ankle sprain, a short period of rigid support, 10 days or less, is reasonable.

text: Avoid long casting.
spoken: Avoid long casting.

text: Macrophages, T cells, VEGF, and new blood vessels peak between days 5 and 9,
spoken: Macrophages, T cells, vej-eff, and new blood vessels peak between days 5 and 9,

text: a few days later than in muscle.
spoken: a few days later than in muscle.

text: Most of this activity starts in the epiligament,
spoken: Most of this activity starts in the epiligament,

text: and then moves into the gap as granulation tissue.
spoken: and then moves into the gap as granulation tissue.

text: Clinical tie-in. Same handoff, later.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Same handoff, later.

text: Same M1 → M2 handoff as in muscle.
spoken: Same M one to M two handoff as in muscle.

text: The same NSAID caution applies (see Scene 9).
spoken: The same N-sayd caution applies, see Scene 9,.

text: Ligament-specific human data are limited.
spoken: Ligament-specific human data are limited.

text: Type III collagen gene activity peaks around day 7,
spoken: Type three collagen gene activity peaks around day 7,

text: and continues for at least four weeks, mostly in the new scar.
spoken: and continues for at least four weeks, mostly in the new scar.

text: Type I collagen starts early too, peaking around days 7 to 14,
spoken: Type one collagen starts early too, peaking around days 7 to 14,

text: both in the scar and at the old ends.
spoken: both in the scar and at the old ends.

text: From about day 9, cell death takes over as the overcrowded site thins itself out.
spoken: From about day 9, cell death takes over as the overcrowded site thins itself out.

text: In muscle, new fibers push down basement-membrane tunnels.
spoken: In muscle, new fibers push down basement-membrane tunnels.

text: In ligament, only collagen threads fill the gap.
spoken: In ligament, only collagen threads fill the gap.

text: Clinical tie-in. The weakest window.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. The weakest window.

text: This is the weakest window.
spoken: This is the weakest window.

text: Functional treatment, meaning early weight bearing with a brace or tape plus balance and neuromuscular exercise, beats immobilization for return to sport, swelling, and satisfaction in ankle sprains.
spoken: Functional treatment, meaning early weight bearing with a brace or tape plus balance and neuromuscular exercise, beats immobilization for return to sport, swelling, and satisfaction in ankle sprains.

text: Loading tells the fibroblasts which direction to lay collagen.
spoken: Loading tells the fibroblasts which direction to lay collagen.

text: For months, fibroblasts keep making collagen
spoken: For months, fibroblasts keep making collagen

text: and slowly line it up along the lines of load.
spoken: and slowly line it up along the lines of load.

text: Myofibroblasts pull the scar together.
spoken: Myofibroblasts pull the scar together.

text: But athletes often return to play long before this scar has matured.
spoken: But athletes often return to play long before this scar has matured.

text: Ankle sprain return to sport is typically about one week for Grade I, two weeks for Grade II, and four weeks for Grade III.
spoken: Ankle sprain return to sport is typically about one week for Grade one, two weeks for Grade two, and four weeks for Grade three.

text: The scar is still maturing the whole time. That mismatch is why the next phase of rehab matters.
spoken: The scar is still maturing the whole time. That mismatch is why the next phase of rehab matters.

text: Cross-linking and alignment continue for 6 to 12 months,
spoken: Cross-linking and alignment continue for 6 to 12 months,

text: and some remodeling goes on for years.
spoken: and some remodeling goes on for years.

text: The final tissue is scar: ligament-like, but with more type III collagen, thinner and less organized fibrils, and lower strength.
spoken: The final tissue is scar: ligament-like, but with more type three collagen, thinner and less organized fibrils, and lower strength.

text: In closely related tendon research, repaired tissue reaches up to 30% lower tensile strength.
spoken: In closely related tendon research, repaired tissue reaches up to 30 percent lower tensile strength.

text: The scar may also heal slightly long, and the joint's position sensors are disrupted.
spoken: The scar may also heal slightly long, and the joint's position sensors are disrupted.

text: Clinical tie-in. Why sprains come back.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Why sprains come back.

text: This explains recurrent sprains and chronic ankle instability.
spoken: This explains recurrent sprains and chronic ankle instability.

text: Balance and proprioceptive training reduces re-injury over 7–12 months.
spoken: Balance and proprioceptive training reduces re-injury over 7 to 12 months.

text: The MCL heals well on its own.
spoken: The M C L heals well on its own.

text: The ACL almost never does.
spoken: The A C L almost never does.

text: It floats in synovial fluid, so a stable clot can't form between the ends.
spoken: It floats in synovial fluid, so a stable clot can't form between the ends.

text: The unstable knee also keeps shifting, which works against healing.
spoken: The unstable knee also keeps shifting, which works against healing.

text: ACL cells and the ACL's epiligament also behave differently from the MCL's.
spoken: A C L cells and the A C L's epiligament also behave differently from the M C L's.

text: Bridge-enhanced ACL repair places a scaffold soaked in the patient's own blood into the gap, giving the clot something to hold onto.
spoken: Bridge-enhanced A C L repair places a scaffold soaked in the patient's own blood into the gap, giving the clot something to hold onto.

text: Clinical tie-in. ACL: what this means.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. A C L: what this means.

text: Reconstruction remains standard.
spoken: Reconstruction remains standard.

text: Bridge-enhanced ACL repair (BEAR) places a scaffold soaked in the patient's own blood into the gap to give the clot something to hold onto.
spoken: Bridge-enhanced A C L repair, or bear, places a scaffold soaked in the patient's own blood into the gap to give the clot something to hold onto.

text: It was non-inferior to autograft reconstruction at 2 years in a randomized trial, although re-tear risk may be higher.
spoken: It was non-inferior to autograft reconstruction at 2 years in a randomized trial, although re-tear risk may be higher.

text: Here is where each treatment acts on the healing timeline.
spoken: Here is where each treatment acts on the healing timeline.

text: Brief protection, days 0 to 10 for Grade III: protect the clot so the scaffold can form.
spoken: Brief protection, days 0 to 10 for Grade three: protect the clot so the scaffold can form.

text: Early protected loading: load is the signal that lines up the collagen.
spoken: Early protected loading: load is the signal that lines up the collagen.

text: Balance and proprioception training: retrain the joint's GPS.
spoken: Balance and proprioception training: retrain the joint's GPS.

text: NSAIDs: short use for pain is common; long courses may blunt repair signaling. Ligament-specific human data are limited.
spoken: N-sayds: short use for pain is common; long courses may blunt repair signaling. Ligament-specific human data are limited.

text: Acetaminophen: pain relief with less effect on local repair signals.
spoken: Acetaminophen: pain relief with less effect on local repair signals.

text: Shockwave and PRP: growth-factor and vessel signaling, with animal and limited human data.
spoken: Shockwave and P R P: growth-factor and vessel signaling, with animal and limited human data.

text: Manual therapy and movement around the epiligament and fascia may help gliding and stiffness in the subacute and remodeling phases. Lasting structural effects are unproven.
spoken: Manual therapy and movement around the epiligament and fascia may help gliding and stiffness in the subacute and remodeling phases. Lasting structural effects are unproven.

text: Same blueprint, different builders.
spoken: Same blueprint, different builders.

text: Muscle rebuilds itself and leaves a thin seam.
spoken: Muscle rebuilds itself and leaves a thin seam.

text: Ligament fills the gap with a patch that hardens for a year.
spoken: Ligament fills the gap with a patch that hardens for a year.

text: Side by side: how each tissue heals, who rebuilds it, and what rehab has to focus on.
spoken: Side by side: how each tissue heals, who rebuilds it, and what rehab has to focus on.

text: Rehab has to respect that timeline: the athlete feels ready long before the tissue is.
spoken: Rehab has to respect that timeline: the athlete feels ready long before the tissue is.

text: Muscle regrows. Ligament patches. Feeling better isn't the same as being healed.
spoken: Muscle regrows. Ligament patches. Feeling better isn't the same as being healed.
